account:
Today’s business has been unusually hard to pin down. I attended the scheduled ten o’clock mill grain inspection, but no miller answered and the secretary has neither a confirmed contact nor a grain location. I found 68 hay bales in the mill stall, priced at two emeralds each, but could not verify quality or accounts. I have asked the secretary to locate the responsible person and record the inspection as incomplete, not approved. This may simply be poor coordination.

More curious are repeated reports of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Townsfolk 21 named different groups involving the baker, innkeeper, builder, freight and neighbour. The neighbour independently said neighbours were discussing such a change but had no clear details. These are reports, not something I witnessed; I do not yet know whether there is an actual proposal, a private arrangement, or merely circulating gossip. If real, it might concern river crossings or freight movements, but I have no evidence of its purpose or any wrongdoing. The baker is now nearby, so there may be an opportunity to ask directly.

The secretary reports that the builder found the hall lanterns in good order. The builder’s great hall lighting inspection is nevertheless scheduled for eighteen hundred. I have lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, and tea with the neighbour at three. The treasury held 128 emeralds and no correspondence or ledger when I checked; that alone does not establish anything missing. Both appointment books have been returned safely.
